RDPLauncher 1.0.1 connects without the Remote Desktop security warning, stops waiting on Remote
Desktop's display list every time, and lets you name your computers.

## Fixed

- **No more "Caution: Unknown remote connection" for computers added by name.** Since the April
  2026 Windows update, Remote Desktop shows that warning every time an .rdp file is opened, so
  RDPLauncher now connects to them like typing the computer into Remote Desktop Connection
  (`mstsc /v`), with the displays set in Remote Desktop Connection's own settings (`Default.rdp`;
  a copy from before RDPLauncher first changed it is kept in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RDPLauncher`).
  Computers added from a saved .rdp file still get the warning; add them by name to avoid it.
- **No more wait and "Display numbers guessed" on every connection.** Remote Desktop's display
  numbers are read once and remembered until your displays change, and reading them is more
  robust. If they still can't be read, it says so once, guesses them the way Remote Desktop
  appears to number displays, and writes what it found to
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RDPLauncher\display-numbers.log`. **Read display numbers again** in the
  right-click menu asks again.

## Changed

- **Rename** the current computer from the right-click menu. The widget shows the name over the
  computer's address, or just the address when it has no name.
- **Clicking the computer** on the widget goes to the next of your computers (scrolling still works).
- The widget no longer shows "Remote Desktop" under the address, and the right-click menu no longer
  repeats the display buttons or has **In a window** (`--displays window` on the command line still
  does that).

## Updating

Exit the running copy (right-click the widget → **Exit**), replace RDPLauncher.exe with the new one
and start it. Your computers and display buttons are kept.
